title.rendered: Wait for What the Father Promised: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: Wait for what the Father promised. The instruction was for ten days in an upper room. The promise has long since come. You are walking in what they received.

content.rendered:
Wait for what the Father promised. The instruction was for ten days in an upper room two thousand years ago. The promise has long since come. You are not waiting for what they waited for. You are walking in what they received.

The Gospel For Today | Wednesday, May 20, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“As they met and ate meals together, he told them that they were on no account to leave Jerusalem but ‘must wait for what the Father promised: the promise you heard from me. John baptized in water; you’ll be baptized in the Holy Spirit—and soon.’”
Acts 1:4–5 (MSG)

Today’s Message

The risen Jesus is eating with His disciples. Forty days have passed since the empty tomb. The ascension is hours away. He has every right to give them a sprawling final sermon. Instead He gives them a single instruction. Wait.

Not go preach. Not plant churches. Not change the world. Wait. Stay in Jerusalem. Hold your position. The Father has promised something and you are not going to make it happen by your striving. You will receive it by His giving.

That single word reshapes everything that comes next in the book of Acts. The first lesson of the new covenant is that the whole thing is gift. The Spirit cannot be earned. The Spirit cannot be conjured by intensity, scheduled by strategy, or hurried by zeal. The Spirit can only be received from a Father who has already decided to give Him.

So they waited. We know now it was ten days. Forty days from resurrection to ascension. Fifty days from Passover to Pentecost. Ten days in the upper room of expectation and prayer and community. Then the day came. The wait ended. The Spirit fell. And the church was born.

Here is where the gospel meets you this morning. You are not waiting for what the disciples waited for. The Father has kept the promise. The Spirit was poured out. He has not been recalled. If you belong to Christ today, the fullness you might be reaching for is already yours. The presence you might be asking God to send is already with you. The waiting in that sense is over.

But there is still something the ten days teach us. They waited together. They waited in prayer. They waited expecting. You and I do not wait for the Spirit to arrive—He is here—but we can still wait expectantly for what He wants to do in us and through us today. That is a different posture, and a good one. Not waiting for God to start. Waiting on God to lead.

Prayer

Father, thank You for keeping every promise You ever made. The Spirit You said You would pour out has been poured out. The fullness You said You would give has been given. I am not chasing something far off. I am walking in what You have already done. Help me wait on You today not as one anxious for arrival but as one already held. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am not waiting for what the disciples waited for. The Spirit has already been poured out. The promise has already come. I walk in the fullness today. My waiting is not for God to start. My waiting is on God to lead. The presence is now and the promise is mine.

  • Acts 1:12–14: How they waited in the upper room
